s1.syndrome_frame: Postoperative spinal infection with neurological deficits
salient_findings: Cervical wound erythema with pus and saliva discharge
Lumbar spinal tenderness and bilateral leg weakness
Enterobacter cloacae cultured from wound and blood
key_facts: Diagnosed with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
Developed cervical wound erythema with pus and saliva discharge on postoperative day 4
Underwent salvage reconstruction with free jejunal autograft and pectoralis major muscle flap coverage
Developed worsening low back pain and fever 15 days after reconstruction
Had lumbar spinal tenderness and bilateral leg weakness
MRI of lumbar spine demonstrated decreased T1 signal and increased T2 and STIR signal at L4–L5

Enterobacter cloacae cultured from wound and blood

differentials: Infectious discitis due to Edwardsiella tarda
per_call: Infectious discitis due to Edwardsiella tarda

shortlist.label: Spondylodiscitis
shortlist.why_kept: Decreased T1 signal and increased T2 and STIR signal at L4–L5 on MRI, consistent with disc infection

shortlist.label: Epidural abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Lumbar spinal tenderness, bilateral leg weakness, and fever, suggesting an abscess compressing the spinal cord

shortlist.label: Osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Enterobacter cloacae cultured from blood, suggesting a bone infection

shortlist.label: Spinal epidural abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Neurological deficits and fever, consistent with an abscess in the spinal epidural space

shortlist.label: Enterobacter cloacae vertebral osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Enterobacter cloacae cultured from blood and previous history of infection, making this a likely cause of vertebral osteomyelitis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of worsening low back pain, fever, and lumbar spinal tenderness, combined with the MRI findings of decreased T1 signal and increased T2 and STIR signal at L4–L5, are consistent with spondylodiscitis, an infection of the intervertebral disc and adjacent vertebrae. The presence of Enterobacter cloacae in the blood cultures also supports this diagnosis, as it is a known cause of spondylodiscitis.

rejected.label: Epidural abscess
rejected.why: While the patient has symptoms of back pain and fever, the MRI findings do not specifically indicate an epidural abscess, which would typically appear as a collection of pus outside the dura mater.

rejected.label: Osteomyelitis
rejected.why: Osteomyelitis is a broader term that refers to any infection of the bone, but the patient's symptoms and MRI findings are more specific to spondylodiscitis, which affects the intervertebral disc and adjacent vertebrae.

rejected.label: Spinal epidural abscess
rejected.why: Similar to epidural abscess, the MRI findings do not specifically indicate a spinal epidural abscess, and the patient's symptoms are more consistent with spondylodiscitis.

rejected.label: Enterobacter cloacae vertebral osteomyelitis
rejected.why: While Enterobacter cloacae is the causative organism, the term 'vertebral osteomyelitis' is too broad and does not specifically capture the patient's condition, which is more accurately described as spondylodiscitis.
